forecaster_note: Sth magnets seeing a bump of size with S swell on its way. Clean morning, afternoon texture. There's a little bit of long range S swell which will show its face mid-morning. Expect small, clean and full conditions at dawn, then as the tide works its way out, a few larger chest high sets should emerge. We're in for some NE onshores in the afternoon, so head to the Sth facing beaches / Nth corners to grab the new size and the cleanest conditions — the exposed stretches will be fairly chopped up. — Anthony Spinks, Surfline

wind.summary: Glassy W/WNW offshore under 5 kph until ~11am, then NE onshore 11–16 kph shuts it down from midday

shark.summary: Two SLSNSW drone sightings yesterday morning (Sat 22 Aug) — Shelly Beach 8:10am and Mona Vale 8:45am, both with water evacuated. Nothing new overnight; feed is live (latest statewide detection 14.5h old, 7 in the past 24h). Shelly sits right around the Manly headland — stay switched on there.

days.label: Today
days.note: The S groundswell landed — 5.6ft @ 9s from 182°, peaking at 505 kJ at dawn and bleeding down to 149 kJ by midday. Dead south is the wrong door for Dee Why, so the size is at Long Reef and Curl Curl. Offshore and glassy until ~11am, then NE onshore. Go now.

dee-why.window: 7–10:30am while the W offshore holds and the tide drains to the 10:00am low. Point is your best shot — the beachie will be closing out on that S angle.
alerts: Dead S at 182° — wraps badly into Dee Why, expect the bay to feel half the size it is next door

tip.label: Frontside at the Point
tip.text: 100/100 consistency and 333 kJ at 9am means sets keep coming — but the S angle robs the bay. Sit tight on the Point for the frontside right rather than paddling around the beachie hunting a bank that isn't lined up.

long-reef.window: Pick of the day. 6–11am — biggest, cleanest, and the only spot properly exposed to the 182° line. Chest to a foot overhead on the sets.

tip.label: Backside on the lefts
tip.text: The south swell runs down the reef and throws lefts — backside for you. 505 kJ at 6am dropping to 149 by noon, so the early is genuinely a different wave to the late. Don't sleep in.

curl-curl.window: Strong second option. 7–11am, north corner for the cleanest water. Punchy chest-to-head on the banks — exactly your bracket.

tip.label: North corner
tip.text: Spinks says head to south-facing beaches and north corners today. Curl Curl's north end is the shelter play once the NE fills in — it'll hold shape 30–45 min longer than the open stretch.

manly.window: Skip it today unless you want a soft one — half the size of Long Reef with the same wind clock.
alerts: ⚠️ Shark: drone sighting at Shelly Beach 8:10am Sat 22 Aug, water evacuated

tip.label: Not today
tip.text: Same 333 kJ arriving but the headland eats the S angle — 2–3ft thigh-high while Long Reef is chest to overhead. Drive the extra 10 minutes.

days.label: Tomorrow
days.note: Swell backs off hard — 3ft @ 11s from 181°, energy down to 101 kJ. N/NNW cross-shore at dawn, gusty NE 20 kph by afternoon. A dawn-patrol-or-nothing day, and only Long Reef really holds.

dee-why.window: 6–9am before the NNW cross-shore adds texture. Marginal.
alerts: Drops to poor-fair by midday as the NE builds

long-reef.window: Best of a quiet day. 6–10am — waist to shoulder on the exposed banks with 93% consistency.

curl-curl.window: 6–9:30am. Fades to poor-fair once the NE swings in after midday.

manly.window: Not worth the trip — poor-fair from 9am onwards.

days.label: Weekend
days.note: Another S pulse for the coming weekend. Sat 29 is the bigger day (up to 291 kJ, 6ft @ 8s from 175°) but a S cross-shore fills in from 10am. Sun 30 is smaller and cleaner with W offshore right through to noon — that's the session to plan around. Confidence still low (37–75%), so re-check midweek.

dee-why.window: Sun 30, 7–11am — W offshore 5–7 kph the whole morning. Sat 29 has more push but S cross-shore from 10am.
alerts: Swell still ~175–178° — same bad S wrap for the bay
Forecast confidence only 37–75% this far out

long-reef.window: Again the pick. Sat 29 mid-morning for size (4–6ft, chest to a foot overhead), Sun 30 for clean W offshore and 4–5ft.

curl-curl.window: Sun 30 morning is the cleaner half. Sat 29 slips to poor-fair once the S cross-shore hits 17 kph mid-morning.

manly.window: Sat 29 mid-morning is the one day Manly gets to 3–4ft. Otherwise thigh-to-waist.
